behavior: Usually solitary and territorial; watches from exposed waterside perches or hovers, then plunges headfirst for fish and other aquatic prey. Flies along shorelines with a loud rattling call and excavates nesting burrows in earthen banks.
field_marks: Stocky, top-heavy profile with a large head and shaggy crest
Long, thick, straight dark bill and dark eye
White collar and underparts with a broad blue-gray breast band; females add a rusty belly band and flanks
Fine white spotting and barring on the wings and medium-length, square-tipped tail
Short legs with small orange-gray feet
habitat: Clear or calm streams, rivers, ponds, lakes, estuaries, and coastal waters with open hunting perches; exposed earthen banks are important for nesting.
